112518.y_answer: \text{The electronic structure of coordination compounds—encompassing ligand field splitting (Δ), d-electron configuration, spin state, oxidation state, and π-back-donation—directly determines their spectroscopic properties. UV-Vis spectroscopy probes d-d transitions (e.g., [Co(H₂O)₆]²⁺ pink vs. [CoCl₄]²⁻ blue) and charge transfer bands (e.g., [MnO₄]⁻ LMCT at 520 nm). IR spectroscopy detects changes in bond order via back-donation (e.g., ν(CO) shifts from 2090 cm⁻¹ in [Mn(CO)₆]⁺ to 1879 cm⁻¹ in [Mn(CO)₆]⁻). NMR spectroscopy reflects spin state through paramagnetic shifts (e.g., high-spin [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺ with S = 2 shows 100s of ppm shifts vs. diamagnetic [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ with S = 0) and coordination effects on ligand chemical shifts (e.g., ¹³C(CO) at 205 ppm in [Ni(CO)₄] vs. 183 ppm for free CO).}
